chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and Dhū al-Ḥijjah. Whoever intends hajj should let his hair grow when he sights the crescent of Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and whoever intends ʿumrah should let his hair grow for a month.

key_terms.أَشْهُرٌ مَعْلُومَاتٌ: specified and recognized months for hajj
key_terms.ذُو ٱلْحِجَّةِ: the month of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, the final hajj month
key_terms.ذُو ٱلْقَعْدَةِ: the month of Dhū al-Qaʿdah, one of the hajj months
key_terms.شَوَّالٌ: the month of Shawwāl, the first of the hajj months
key_terms.هِلَالِ: the crescent marking the beginning of the month
key_terms.وَفَّرَ شَعْرَهُ: he should let his hair grow and leave it uncut

ai.seo_question: What are the well-known months of hajj, and when should a pilgrim begin letting the hair grow?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic phrase about the well-known months of hajj as Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and Dhū al-Ḥijjah. It also gives a practical ruling for one intending hajj or ʿumrah: to let the hair grow beginning from the relevant time before entering the rites.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2520 - Mu‘awiyah ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"The Hajj is in well-known months" (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:197)

—Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa‘dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. Whoever intends to perform Hajj should let their hair grow from the sighting of the crescent of Dhu al-Qa‘dah. Whoever intends to perform ‘Umrah should let their hair grow for a month."
